scenes.headline: How a decision model ignores the order of its options
scenes.sub: AgentJev-0.6B: a shared prefix, private branches, and a head with no positions.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Quince! AgentJev picks between an agent's options. Here's how it ignores their order, yet lets them talk.

scenes.label: The idea
scenes.text: Encode the shared state once, give every option a private branch, then let the options meet only in a head with no positions.
scenes.say: Encode the shared state once, give each option a private branch, then let options meet only in a small head with no positions.

scenes.title: One prefix, many branches, one set head

steps.note: 92.4% fewer backbone tokens, 2.04x on the clock
steps.say: The state and the question are encoded once and cached.

steps.note: every branch resumes at the same position index
steps.say: Each option gets its own copy of that cache. No option sees another, and every one starts at the same position.
Each branch comes out as one vector. Only now do the options meet, in a two-layer transformer with no positional embeddings.
A scorer reads one number per option. Nothing anywhere records which slot an option arrived in.

scenes.title: What the shared prefix saves
scenes.credit: the repository's own figure; its 255-candidate footer is unmeasured

steps.say: The repository's own figure. Without sharing, all sixty-four options recompute the state: over thirty-three thousand backbone tokens.
Shared, about two and a half thousand: exactly ninety-two point four percent fewer. On the clock, two point oh four times faster.

scenes.title: The one additive term
scenes.say: The set head's output is added onto each option's own vector.

parts.say: The first term is each option, read alone.

parts.note: what knowing the rest of the set adds
parts.say: The second is what knowing the rest of the set adds.

parts.note: zero the second term: a plain per-option scorer
parts.say: Zero the second term, and it's a plain per-option scorer.

scenes.title: Position carries nothing, content still counts

left.title: Shuffle the list
left.say: Shuffle the list: across two thousand five hundred and twenty permutations, no answer changed, and no logit moved past the float's last bits.

right.title: Change who is on it
right.say: Change which other options are on it, and a logit moves a median of zero point zero eight eight. The options interact.

scenes.text: Isolate options in the backbone, let them meet in a head without positions: order carries nothing, content still counts.

recap: One cached prefix, one private branch per option
Options meet only in a set encoder
scenes.say: To recap: a shared prefix, private branches, and a position-free head where options meet.
